vars.STYLE: Art style: hand-painted anime feature film look. Semi-realistic and painterly, watercolour-and-gouache rendering with soft visible brush texture, delicate thin ink lines, realistic proportions, natural facial features with gentle anime stylisation, soft natural lighting, muted desaturated natural colour grading, subtle film grain. Characters and background rendered as ONE painting. Refined; not chibi, not cartoonish, not photographic, no oversaturation.
vars.PANEL: This is a single cinematic comic panel, not a character sheet: the character sheets are identity references only, so do not copy their grey background, layout or poses. Keep every character's face, hair, clothing and proportions exactly as on their sheet. Keep important content slightly away from the image edges, because the panel will be cropped a little. Leave a calm, uncluttered area near the top-left for a caption to be added later. No speech bubbles, no captions, no text except the shop sign, no watermark.
vars.WEI: Wei is a lean Chinese (Hakka) man with a single small mole below his RIGHT eye (viewer's left), shown on his character sheet.
vars.SMRITI: Smriti is an Indo-Mauritian woman with warm brown skin, large dark eyes and thick eyebrows, shown on her character sheet.
vars.UNCLE: Uncle Lam is a wiry Chinese shopkeeper with short grey hair, thick black-rimmed glasses and a pencil behind his ear, shown on his character sheet.
vars.FATHER: Mr Ramdass is Smriti's father, a round-faced Indo-Mauritian man with a moustache, shown on his character sheet.
vars.NORELIGION: Purely cultural and social: no religious symbols, rites, altars, statues or temples.

jobs.prompt: Show this exact same shop from the exact same camera position, angle, lens and framing, 12 years later, in 1984. KEEP UNCHANGED: the building's footprint, shape, size and position; the row of four doors; the position of the signboard; the position of the frangipani tree; the cane fields; the distant mountain range and the tall boulder-topped peak; the sky composition; the art style and muted colour grading. CHANGES: (1) the rough basalt walls are now plastered smooth and painted a pale cream-yellow; a few grey basalt blocks still show at one lower corner where the plaster has chipped; (2) the four doors are freshly repainted deep red; (3) the rusty roof and awning are replaced by newer grey corrugated sheets; (4) the old crooked signboard is replaced by a larger, professionally painted dark green signboard with gold lettering, still reading 'LAM STORE' and 林記; (5) two red paper lanterns hang under the awning; (6) the frangipani is now a young tree about twice the height of the door, with a small rounded canopy in bloom; (7) the dirt road is now a narrow, slightly worn tarmac road; (8) a wooden electricity pole with wires stands at the roadside to the right; (9) a small concrete house with a tin roof appears in the distance among the fields. Warm late-afternoon light. No people. No text other than the sign. No watermark.

The first image is a background plate of the shop in 1984. The second image is the character sheet of Uncle Lam. {UNCLE} KEEP the building, sign, tree, road, mountains and camera angle exactly as in the plate. Change the time to early evening dusk: a deep blue sky with the last warm glow on the horizon. Strings of small warm light bulbs run from the shop's awning across the road to the electricity pole and glow softly. Guests of every Mauritian community (Indo-Mauritian, Creole, Sino-Mauritian; old and young, in their best 1980s clothes) walk along the road toward the shop in small groups, carrying covered dishes and baskets; two children run ahead. Uncle Lam stands at the open doors in a clean white shirt, welcoming them with a small bow. Festive but gentle mood. Leave calm sky at the top-left for a caption. {NORELIGION} {PANEL} {STYLE}

The images are character sheets of Wei aged 26 ({WEI}), Smriti aged 24 ({SMRITI}), Uncle Lam ({UNCLE}) and Mr Ramdass ({FATHER}). Scene: their wedding party in the backyard behind the shop, 1984, at night. Long tables with white cloths, plates of food, strings of warm bulbs and paper lanterns overhead, banana trees and a tin-roofed shed in the background. In the background centre, Wei (crisp white shirt, flower pinned to it) and Smriti (red silk saree with gold border, jasmine flowers in her hair) sit side by side at the head table, laughing together. In the foreground, Uncle Lam on the left and Mr Ramdass on the right stand facing each other and shake hands firmly, both half-smiling, like two proud fathers sizing each other up. Guests of all Mauritian communities chat at the tables. Leave calm space above the two men's heads for speech bubbles. {NORELIGION} {PANEL} {STYLE}

The images are character sheets of Wei ({WEI}), Smriti ({SMRITI}) and their son (the little boy on the third sheet, here about 2 years old). Scene: Chinatown in Port Louis, Mauritius, during Spring Festival, 1988, daytime. A narrow street of old two-storey colonial shophouses with wooden balconies, rows of red paper lanterns strung overhead, red and gold decorations, a dense happy crowd of every Mauritian community. In the middle of the street a vivid red-and-gold lion dance: the lion rears up with its big eyes and fringed mane while drummers play. In the foreground, Wei carries his little son on his shoulders; the boy shrieks with delight and points at the lion. Beside them Smriti laughs with her head thrown back, clapping. Confetti and a little firecracker smoke drift in the air. Leave calm space in the top-left for a caption. {NORELIGION} {PANEL} {STYLE}

The images are character sheets of Wei ({WEI}) and Smriti ({SMRITI}). Scene: a small, cosy home kitchen in 1980s Mauritius, afternoon light through a window with a curtain, steel pots on a gas ring, jars of spices and a bamboo steamer on the shelf. Wei and Smriti stand side by side at a wooden table covered in flour. Smriti, sleeves rolled up, holds a rolling pin and a thin round flatbread (dholl puri), pointing at Wei's dough with a playful scolding look. Wei, flour on his cheek and apron, holds up a small hand-pleated dumpling and grins back at her teasingly. Between them a plate of neat dumplings and a plate of flatbreads; a bowl of yellow split-pea filling. Warm, playful, intimate mood. Leave calm space above their heads for speech bubbles. {PANEL} {STYLE}

The first image is the inside of the shop in 1972. Show the SAME shop interior in 1990: the same layout, counter and shelves, but the walls are now plastered and painted cream, the shelves are fuller with colourful 1990s packaging (no readable brand names), a small electric fan and a calendar on the wall, a fluorescent tube light. The other images are character sheets of Wei ({WEI}) and his two children (a 6-year-old boy in a striped T-shirt, a 3-year-old girl with two bunches). Scene: lively afternoon. Wei's two children and three neighbourhood kids of different Mauritian backgrounds race through the aisle in a game of chase, laughing; a sack of rice wobbles. Behind the counter, Wei laughs out loud with his head tipped back, one hand on the old brass scale. Dynamic, joyful, a little chaotic. Leave calm space in the top-left for a caption. {PANEL} {STYLE}

The first image is the shop. The other images are character sheets: Wei ({WEI}), Smriti ({SMRITI}), their two children (boy 6, girl 3), Uncle Lam ({UNCLE}) and Mr Ramdass ({FATHER}). Scene: Spring Festival morning, 1990, a group photograph in front of the shop. The camera is a little closer than the plate, framing the open red doors, the sign and the frangipani tree; plain red paper strips with gold patterns (no writing) hang on both sides of the doors, two red lanterns above. Everyone faces the camera in a posed photo: in the centre, Uncle Lam, now about 76, sits on a wooden chair holding a walking cane, smiling; behind him stand Wei and Smriti, her hand on his shoulder; the two children sit cross-legged in front; to one side Mr Ramdass, grey-haired, with his wife, an Indo-Mauritian woman in a pale saree; on the other side, about five neighbours of different Mauritian communities squeeze into the frame, one making bunny ears behind another's head. Warm morning light, joyful and slightly chaotic. Leave calm space at the top-left for a caption. {NORELIGION} {PANEL} {STYLE}
